blind_spots: No account-level concentration summary across duplicate holdings and funds.
No option premium, expiry, or max-loss budget for protective structures.
Tax basis still pending, limiting judgment on taxable trim efficiency and wash-sale consequences.
incoherences: SPCX is 'not decomposed' yet a covered-call advisory is still proposed.
DXCM is held despite weakening evidence, yet also targeted for both puts and calls.
PSQ rationale cites tech-led deterioration but also leans on Industrials exposure, muddying hedge logic.
memo.strongest_objection: The desk is treating a mixed, late-cycle tape as justification for a broad menu of hedges, calls, shorts, and inverse exposure. That risks death-by-overlays: paying option decay, capping rebounds, and adding whipsaw exposure when simpler trims-to-cash already satisfy the defensive mandate more cleanly.
top_concerns: Option overlays lack explicit cost/tenor discipline; retirement hedging can become expensive drift.
Several HOLD labels understate weakening evidence; watch posture is missing on opaque or slipping names.
Desk may be over-extrapolating mixed breadth weakness into too many overlays rather than prioritizing trims and cash.

verdicts.missed_risk: Put cost bleed and over-hedging if Industrials stabilize.
verdicts.reason: Constitution-allowed IRA hedge on a lagging sector, but no premium/tenor guardrails shown. Protective puts help, yet cost discipline matters in a mixed tape, not a confirmed breakdown.

verdicts.missed_risk: Basis unknown; re-entry timing may lag a sharp reversal.
verdicts.reason: Core trim respects never-full-exit and 50% stays within the 60% cap. ARKX is concentrated, lagging, and ladder-fired; reducing exposure fits a defensive retirement mandate.

verdicts.missed_risk: Breadth may improve before put cost pays off.
verdicts.reason: Allowed hedge on a fully lagging sector, but materials breadth at 61% weakens the urgency versus pure breakdown conditions. Hedge may be sensible, yet needs pricing discipline.

verdicts.missed_risk: Single-name gap risk exists, but blanket hedging may be inefficient.
verdicts.reason: Healthcare is weakening, not lagging, and RS20 is still positive. A full protective put overlay on a smaller non-core position looks expensive relative to the evidence.

verdicts.missed_risk: Watch wash-sale interactions in taxable if any scraps are losses.
verdicts.reason: Janitorial cleanup is constitution-consistent and explicitly cleanup-exempt. Consolidating immaterial scraps can reduce clutter without changing strategic posture.

verdicts.missed_risk: Undefined option structures can smuggle excess risk or cost.
verdicts.reason: Designer-live placeholder is acceptable in SHADOW, but not reviewable as advice because structure, strikes, tenor, and max cost are absent.

verdicts.missed_risk: Whipsaw risk if tech rebounds from oversold conditions.
verdicts.reason: Whitelisted inverse ETF and tech weakness support the concept, but the trigger is narrow and book rationale mixes tech-led weakness with industrial exposure. Size band is broad for a mixed tape.

verdicts.missed_risk: China/EV headline squeezes can outrun a tight stop.
verdicts.reason: Fits taxable-short constitution: price above $10,000 short float below 10%, stop within 10%, position cap explicit, held-symbol prohibition not contradicted by provided facts.

verdicts.missed_risk: Consumer discretionary oversold bounces can be violent.
verdicts.reason: Passes the taxable-short rule set and is positioned in a lagging industry with controlled stop distance. Reasonable as advisory-only shadow exposure.

verdicts.missed_risk: Rate-cut hopes can squeeze homebuilders sharply higher.
verdicts.reason: Constitution-compliant taxable short: price, float, stop, and size all fit. Industry is lagging, so the advisory is structurally defensible.

verdicts.missed_risk: Assignment risk can impair recovery participation.
verdicts.reason: Covered calls are whitelisted, but on a retirement core-adjacent industrial ETF in a mixed tape they can monetize weakness while sacrificing rebound upside. Fine only with disciplined strike selection.

verdicts.missed_risk: Upside forfeiture if cyclicals mean-revert.
verdicts.reason: Allowed and logical on a lagging sector, but materials breadth is not collapsed. Income may be purchased by capping upside just as a rebound starts.

verdicts.missed_risk: Single-name upside gap after weak period.
verdicts.reason: DXCM is not clearly broken; healthcare RS20 remains positive. Selling calls on a smaller non-core growth name risks capping recovery more than it improves defense.

verdicts.missed_risk: Unknown holdings could be near inflection or event risk.
verdicts.reason: The desk admits no reliable current decomposition, so writing calls anyway is internally inconsistent. If you cannot judge the holding, you should not cap its upside.

verdicts.missed_risk: Defensive crowding can make alternatives unattractive.
verdicts.reason: Trim-watch is acceptable, but SCHD remains income/core-aligned and its largest sector is leading Financials. Watch fits; aggressive trimming would overreact to mixed tape.

verdicts.missed_risk: Option-income funds can lag sharply in rebounds.
verdicts.reason: Trim-watch is the right posture. JEPI is defensive-income oriented, yet a large share sits in weakening/lagging sectors; watchfulness is warranted without immediate aggression.

verdicts.missed_risk: Payment-volume sensitivity if macro deteriorates quickly.
verdicts.reason: Leading sector, above 50DMA, core position. HOLD is the right defensive-desk posture here.

verdicts.missed_risk: Roth concentration not shown; account-level sizing unknown.
verdicts.reason: Same logic as rollover: leading sector and technical support argue for HOLD, especially inside a tax-advantaged core account.

verdicts.missed_risk: FX and non-US sector weakness may be hidden.
verdicts.reason: Refusing to guess is correct, but HOLD on an undecomposed international fund is weaker than neutral-watch. Lack of decomposition should reduce conviction, not imply comfort.

verdicts.missed_risk: Sector breadth could recover before trim triggers.
verdicts.reason: Trim-watch fits. Industrials are lagging, but this is core and constitution forbids full exit. Watch posture is appropriately defensive without forcing action.

verdicts.missed_risk: High-beta tech can reverse despite sector improvement.
verdicts.reason: Technology is improving, so HOLD is defensible, but growth-vs-value is lagging hard. For a retirement desk, this deserves at least a tighter watch rather than complacent hold.

verdicts.missed_risk: Theme funds can snap back sharply after capitulation.
verdicts.reason: Trim is the right posture. Concentration, lagging industrial exposure, and fired ladder escalation support a defensive core reduction without violating the never-full-exit rule.

verdicts.missed_risk: Duration risk if yields back up further.
verdicts.reason: HOLD is sensible. It is fixed income, outside equity-sector mapping, and trims are muted by operator directive. No evidence here argues for changing that stance.

verdicts.missed_risk: Defense/aerospace headlines can trump sector weakness.
verdicts.reason: Trim is appropriate. Pure industrials exposure in a lagging sector with ladder evidence justifies defense, especially for retirement capital.

verdicts.missed_risk: Commodity rebound could change the state quickly.
verdicts.reason: Trim-watch is right. Materials are lagging, but breadth is not disastrous enough to demand immediate trim from the provided facts.

verdicts.missed_risk: Single-name healthcare can break faster than sector averages.
verdicts.reason: HOLD is acceptable, but evidence already says weakening sector and below 50DMA. A watch posture would better match the facts than plain hold.

verdicts.missed_risk: Opaque exposure can hide concentrated cyclicals or growth risk.
verdicts.reason: Not guessing is good, but undecomposed should likely mean watchlist ambiguity, not affirmative HOLD. Muting trims does not create conviction.

verdicts.missed_risk: Tax friction may outweigh modest risk reduction.
verdicts.reason: Trim-watch is fair, but taxable adds basis and wash-sale complexity. The stance is right only if tax drag does not overwhelm the defensive benefit.

verdicts.missed_risk: Value-tech can lag even if sector broadens.
verdicts.reason: Technology improving supports HOLD, but being 4.38% below 50DMA means the name is not clean. Watchful hold is more accurate than plain hold.

verdicts.missed_risk: Oversold rotation rebound risk is underweighted.
verdicts.reason: The tape reads as late-cycle, mixed, breadth-thinning rather than a clean rotation to chase or outright bear collapse. The desk is mostly right, but perhaps too eager on some hedges.

verdicts.missed_risk: Cash can underperform if risk-on returns abruptly.
verdicts.reason: Selling half and parking proceeds in cash is constitutionally clean and fits the stated defensive lean. Cash is appropriate when no destination clearly qualifies.

blind_spots: No cumulative core-trim ledger enforcing the 60% floor + 90-session re-entry across multiple fired tranches.
V held $10,000K + $10,000K across two IRAs = $10,000K single-name; no aggregate concentration flag.
Net portfolio short exposure (PSQ + KTOS + HII + HMY + puts) never summed against 'advisory-only/defensive hedge' intent — could be materially net-short.
incoherences: Desk claims lint clean / no contradictions, yet options cards trade SPCX while its stance says never-guess, and multiple ladders per symbol conflict.
BND trim muted by operator but round_trips still lists BND 'advised' — muted engine still surfacing actions.
memo.strongest_objection: The book's real risk is $10,000K SCHG (46% Tech) + JEPQ (50% Tech) — the desk fiddles with $10,000-31K trims and thin-liquidity options collars while the dominant Tech concentration sits on watch-only. Meanwhile it stacks three overlapping treatments (puts+CCs+trims) on the same small Industrials names and layers four bearish instruments without netting exposure. If this is a bear-market head-fake (growth IMPROVING, NH/NL neutral), the defensive lean sells cyclicals into cash at the wrong moment, locks 90-session re-entry, and the un-summed short stack whipsaws — all while the actual concentration risk goes unaddressed.
top_concerns: Stacked/duplicate ladder tranches (ARKX 45%+35%+T2, XAR 45%+35%, QCOM 55%+60%) lack a cumulative-total guard — core names ARKX/XAR risk breaching the 60% trim cap / de-facto full exit forbidden by registry.

Layered overlapping treatment of single positions: XLI and SPCX each carry protective put + covered call + trim-watch simultaneously — these are undisclosed collars stacked on trim candidates; net cost/greeks never shown.
Options advice on SPCX ('not decomposed — never guess') contradicts the desk's own refusal to analyze it; hedging a black box with 94-IV structures is indefensible.

verdicts.missed_risk: Put premium bleed on a $10,000K position already flagged for trim/exit is wasted cost.
verdicts.reason: Covered protective put on held XLI is IRA-legal and advisory-only. But desk simultaneously trim-watches XLI and shorts defense via KTOS/HII; buying puts atop a trim candidate double-hedges. Pick one.

verdicts.missed_risk: Buying high-IV puts + selling calls simultaneously = collar not disclosed as such; net cost/greeks unstated.
verdicts.reason: IV 76.4 makes puts expensive; hedging a HOLD-rated name via costly puts vs simply trimming is inefficient. Legal and covered, but the CC card on same shares is the cheaper income hedge.

verdicts.missed_risk: Stacked ladder tranches (45%+35%+T2) could full-exit a core position — constitution violation.
verdicts.reason: Core trim 45% within 60% cap, IRA no tax gate. But ladder shows T1 45% AND T2 fired AND separate 35% ladder fired — cumulative trims risk breaching 60% core floor; card shows single tranche only.

verdicts.missed_risk: Aggregate ladder execution may exceed 60% core trim cap without a running-total guard.
verdicts.reason: 45% trim within cap, factor math sound. Same stacked-ladder concern: T1 45% + separate 35% fired + T2 armed. Verify cumulative core reduction stays ≤60%.

verdicts.missed_risk: 94 IV means enormous premium decay; unclear underlying factsheet undermines strike selection.
verdicts.reason: SPCX 'not decomposed, never guess' per stance card, yet IV 94.1 puts advised on it. Covered/legal but hedging an un-analyzable $10,000K position with 94-IV puts is poor cost discipline.

verdicts.missed_risk: Duplicate 55%/60% ladders both fired could over-sell; position tiny ($10,000K residual).
verdicts.reason: 55% trim triggers concentration+giveback correctly. But in_play shows TWO QCOM ladders (55% and 60%) both fired; combined exceeds any single-order logic and position is only $10,000K. Reconcile duplicate ladders.

verdicts.missed_risk: Cleanup must confirm none of the 10 lines are core (cleanup-exempt) before closing.
verdicts.reason: Janitorial consolidation of $10,000K/10 scraps below materiality floor; cleanup-exempt core protection noted. Verify no core registry symbols swept in.
Designer pending, no ticket, n/a direction — nothing to adjudicate. Placeholder is honest.

verdicts.missed_risk: PSQ + ANET/CSCO puts + KTOS/HII shorts stack net-short beyond stated hedge intent.
verdicts.reason: Whitelisted inverse, bounce-only entry disciplined, hard 2-close exit, sized 2-5%. Tech-led deterioration thesis matches tape. Sound tactical hedge.

verdicts.missed_risk: Deep downtrend (-40%) = mean-reversion squeeze risk despite low SF.
verdicts.reason: Taxable-only, SF 5.46%<10%, price≥$10,000 stop 9.7%≤10%, ≤2% book, not held. Meets all short constraints. -40% vs 200DMA is stretched but confirmed pool.

verdicts.missed_risk: KTOS+HII both A&D = single-industry short concentration, not diversified hedge.
verdicts.reason: SF 2.31%, stop 8.0%≤10%, ≥$10,000 ≤2% book, not held, confirmed A&D pool. Compliant. Note PSQ already provides broad hedge — three shorts + inverse is concentrated bearish.

verdicts.missed_risk: Gold rallying on defensive/haven bid contradicts short; low SF amplifies squeeze.
verdicts.reason: Gold miner short while Energy/Materials LEADING/IMPROVING is a counter-tape single-name bet, not a defensive hedge. SF 1.43% ultra-low = squeeze fuel. Compliant but thesis weak vs posture.

verdicts.missed_risk: 10.3% spread + vol 0 means poor execution; $10,000 premium may not clear.
verdicts.reason: Spread 10.3% wide, vol 0, OI 78 — thin liquidity, fill risk real. Caps upside +2.8% on LAGGING name is fine, but combined with protective put = undisclosed collar.

verdicts.missed_risk: CC + protective put on same 200sh = collar; combined greeks/cost not shown.
verdicts.reason: Deep OI 2426, strike +16.1% leaves room, IV 76.4 = rich premium ($10,000). Reasonable income on a HOLD. Note simultaneous put = collar; disclose net structure.

verdicts.missed_risk: Un-decomposed underlying; collar on unknown factsheet is flying blind.
verdicts.reason: IV 94.1 = juicy $10,000 premium, strike +15.7%, OI 88 thin. But SPCX 'not decomposed/never guess' — selling calls on un-analyzable name plus buying puts = full collar on a black box.
Best liquidity (OI 10156, spread 3.7%), strike +6.8%, clean income on LAGGING tech HOLD. Well-constructed.

verdicts.missed_risk: $10,000K single fund is the dominant book risk; watch-only may be too passive if Tech breaks.
verdicts.reason: $10,000K with 46% Tech LAGGING, no fund stop — trim-watch is correct, largest single risk in book. Defensive redeploy path sound.

playbook: 1 · GET IN on BOUNCE days: QQQ up ≥ +0.75% (≥ $10,000) while the trigger state holds — the hedge is at a discount when the index pops. Buy 1/3 per bounce day, never after a big down day (you'd pay up). ALERT armed: 'QQQ bounce — hedge entry window'.
2 · TAKE PROFITS in halves: PSQ +8% (≈ $10,000) → sell half. ALERT armed. PSQ +15% (≈ $10,000) or a capitulation gap-down in QQQ → take the rest. ALERT armed.
3 · STAND DOWN regardless of P&L when the trigger state exits (2-close confirmed) — the hedge's job ended; holding an inverse ETF past its reason bleeds daily-reset decay.
4 · Levels recompute nightly until an entry is recorded (auto-detected from Schwab ingest or your tap on the paper twin).
